trl_reason: The guide documents the principles and methods of the DSAS v5.1 rate calculations with worked examples, and runs the software as a 'controlled test' on sample shoreline data with expected results shown. It reports no validation against independent observations, no acceptance criteria, and no documented operational use of v5.1.

APCTT-C01.quote: DSAS uses a measurement baseline method (Leatherman and Clow, 1983) to calculate rate-of-change statistics for a time series of shorelines.
APCTT-C01.note: States the measurement-baseline and regression/end-point statistical principles behind the rate calculations, citing literature (Leatherman and Clow; Dolan; Crowell; Genz).

APCTT-C02.quote: The distances from the baseline to each intersection point along a transect (fig. 3) are used to compute the selected statistics.
APCTT-C02.note: Describes how the tool works in its application: transects cast from a baseline intersect dated shorelines, and the intersect distances and dates give the change rates.

APCTT-C03.quote: The slope of the equation describing the line is the rate (1.34 meters per year).
APCTT-C03.note: Worked analytical examples show the critical function on a shoreline dataset: an LRR of 1.34 m/yr with LCI95 of 0.50, plus a full numeric summary report.

APCTT-C04.quote: Once the sample dataset has been downloaded and added to ArcMap, the following user settings should be applied to run a controlled test of the sample data.
APCTT-C04.note: By analogy: the v5.1 software is run as a controlled test on sample (test) shoreline datasets, and the resulting rate outputs are shown in figs. 4.2 and 4.4.

APCTT-C05.note: Rates are not calibrated or validated against independent real observations; the sample runs only show expected output, with no accuracy assessment.

APCTT-C06.note: The only applications are tutorial sample-data subsets (Rodanthe NC, Barnstable MA); no real study-area application of v5.1 is reported as a demonstration.

APCTT-C07.note: No statement that v5.1 was used by its intended users for real decisions; the mention of a 'global user base' and of NASC needs is general and not tied to v5.1.

APCTT-C08.note: v5.1 is said to be released and 'tested for compatibility' with ArcGIS 10.4-10.7, but no qualification testing of the rate calculations against requirements is reported.

APCTT-C09.note: The '25 years' of refinement refers to DSAS generally, not routine operational use of v5.1 over a stated period; v5.1 was released in Oct 2021, the same time as the guide.

APCTT-C10.note: No requirements or acceptance criteria are stated and compared with measured performance; sample results are only to be visually matched to the figures.

APCTT-C11.quote: The basic sample data include four shoreline positions for a section of the North Carolina coast near Rodanthe along the Outer Banks and a reference baseline from which the DSAS transects are cast.
APCTT-C11.note: Test conditions are defined: sample shoreline sources, dates and proxies, the ArcGIS geodatabase environment, and run settings (spacing, smoothing, CI, uncertainty) for the released DSAS add-in.

APCTT-C12.quote: Each method used to calculate shoreline rates of change is based on measured differences between shoreline positions through time.
APCTT-C12.note: The cited evidence concerns the DSAS rate-of-change calculations themselves (methods, worked examples and sample-data rate outputs), not a different element or the parent program.
